correctness.rationale: Exact transforming-factor stages reduce to composite trapezoidal/Simpson positive quadratures of a rotating rank-one projector. A finite complex geometric sum yields both spectral formulas, a positive-weight spanning argument gives the precise singular sets, and elementary cosine sign analysis gives the sharp crossover. The fixed-N expansions follow algebraically from Taylor series. A standalone original-stage implementation passed 2940 numerical checks; these do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper introduces both Lyapunov IF-SSPRK methods and proves preservation of symmetry and nonnegative semidefiniteness. Its inspected method equations, numerical section, and conclusions do not give exact oscillator covariance spectra, strict-PD rank-loss sets, or the signed second-versus-third-order minimum-eigenvalue crossover. Earlier integrating-factor and positivity-preserving methods supply tools and distinct guarantees. The older algebra of finite trigonometric sums is not claimed new; the combination is a method-specific spectral and ellipticity classification. Detailed searches found no matching theorem, but priority risk from unindexed sampling/Gramian literature remains.
residual_risks: A classical quadrature-theoretic or sampled-data controllability lemma might imply this exact frequency crossover under different terminology; failure to locate one is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: Strict covariance ellipticity is necessary to invert a numerical reachability Gramian for control energy or covariance-based inference. The exact theorem exhibits false rank deficiency of an otherwise positive-definite continuous Gramian, proves that extra Simpson stages repair all odd-half-turn failures, and identifies when a higher-order method unexpectedly has a smaller minimal eigenvalue than a lower-order one. These are motivated numerical stability boundaries rather than arbitrary parameter substitutions; no broad statement beyond the proved two-dimensional case is claimed.
